verbs.name: screen_record.doctor
verbs.description: Report the SCREEN RECORDER's capability cards (the recorder analog of system.doctor). It also projects the app-local microphone choice: `microphones` contains only short-lived opaque tokens plus generic category-and-ordinal labels, and `microphone_selection` reports System Default, a ready selected source, or an unavailable saved source. Windows and macOS enumerate native endpoint identities privately; Linux is System Default only. No endpoint ID, UID, vendor/friendly name, serial, backend name, auth, or path is public. `warm_mic:true` opens the currently resolved source only for one bounded test; it does not persist or switch a source. No project required.

warm_mic.description: When true, briefly test the current resolved microphone source. It never changes selection, persists a token, opens a competing stream during recording, or returns a native endpoint identity.

mode.description: `check` (default) runs the full check, including a short real screen capture on Windows and macOS that can make the OS show a screen-recording alert; use it only when the person asks to check or starts a recording. `status` reports the same fields without starting any capture or system prompt: the screen card is the last check or not checked yet, and macOS source lists are read only when the OS already allows screen capture. `microphone` reads only the microphone choice and permission, with no screen, window, or camera read.

fps.description: Requested frame rate for the selected recording source; defaults to 30.

monitor.description: Legacy 1-based display index, used only when monitor_id is absent.

monitor_id.description: Opaque current display identity from Doctor; revalidated before the check.

window.description: Opaque current window identity from Doctor; revalidated before the check.

verbs.result: {mode:"check"|"status", screen_check:"checked"|"not_checked"|"permission_needed"|"not_applicable", cards, video_encoder?:{checked:boolean,ready:boolean,reason:string|null,message:string,detail:string|null,width:number|null,height:number|null,fps:number}, ready, start_allowed, monitors:[{id?,index,name,width,height,primary}], windows:[{id,title,app?}], window_capture_supported:boolean, camera:{supported,devices:[{id,label,state,detail}],detail}, scenes:{supported,catalog_revision,layouts,timers,timer_actions,camera_required_layouts,recovery,detail}, pause:{supported,layouts?,streams?,requires?,incompatible,recovery?,detail}, quality:{supported,output_sizes,profiles,detail}, microphones:[{token,label}], microphone_selection:{mode:"system_default"|"selected",label?,status}, mic_warm?} — scenes is passive/path-free and opens no device; Presenter PiP readiness is conditional on an explicitly selected camera. pause is a passive capability: macOS may advertise the bounded exact-display/integer-FPS screen plus optional mic/system-audio owner and its current incompatibility reasons; it never opens a device and Linux/Windows advertise supported:false. camera enumeration is passive and never opens a device or permission prompt; ids are opaque and labels are display-only. A selected camera is used only by the explicit screen_record.start{camera_id} action. `quality.supported` is true only when this compiled backend owns and final-verifies simple Source/1080p/720p plus Standard/High output requests; its lists are empty otherwise and callers must omit `screen_record.start.quality`. On Windows, `video_encoder` reports whether the selected source, dimensions and frame rate can initialize video recording; the `video_encoder` card is ok, degraded, or unknown and contains only the plain message. `status` reads the matching cached check without opening a capture or encoder. An encoder preparation failure uses reason `video_encoder_unavailable` and keeps native details outside the card. A minimized selected window stays minimized and is not checked; `video_encoder.reason` is `window_minimized` and the plain message asks the person to restore it and check again. Only explicit recording Start may restore the window. `window_capture_supported` reports whether the compiled native backend can capture application windows, even when the current window list is empty; Linux portal capture reports false. Windows/macOS window rows carry an opaque live native `windows[].id`; the UI passes the selected id unchanged and capture revalidates it, while title and app remain display-only. Windows/macOS monitor rows include an opaque versioned native `id` only when an exact native identity is available; no surrogate is generated. Pass that `id` unchanged as `screen_record.start.monitor_id` to require a fresh exact revalidation; display name, ordinal, primary status, and dimensions never replace it. The legacy display picker continues to use only `index` when `id` is absent; Linux returns no in-app monitor rows. microphones are generic category-and-ordinal labels and expiring opaque tokens only. microphone_selection status is ready, unavailable, system_default_only, or recovered_corruption. A saved selected source that is absent remains unavailable and blocks mic-enabled start; it never falls back. mic_warm is present only when requested and tests the resolved source. No native endpoint ID/UID, vendor/friendly name, serial, backend name, auth, monitor device path, or filesystem path is returned. In `status` mode, screen_check `not_checked` keeps start_allowed true because Start runs the full check, and `permission_needed` means macOS has not given ShellX Cut screen recording permission (System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording); the screen card detail says so in plain words. `microphone` mode returns only {mode:"microphone", start_allowed, microphone_access:"granted"|"not_determined"|"denied"|"restricted"|"not_applicable", microphone_blocked:{reason,message,suggested_action}|null, microphones, microphone_selection, mic_warm?}; start_allowed there means a voiceover take may start, and microphone_blocked names the missing permission, device or recorder and where the person provides it. `reason` is windows_microphone_access_off, windows_apps_microphone_off or windows_desktop_apps_microphone_off (a Windows privacy switch under Settings > Privacy & security > Microphone is off; microphone_access is then denied), no_microphone_device (Windows lists no microphone), macos_denied, macos_restricted or no_recorder. The `status` and `check` results carry the same microphone_access and microphone_blocked. When a microphone test could not open the device, mic_warm carries reason and message.
